reviewer: Codex primary final critical reading; selected separate-reader findings retained in evidence/reviews. No human/Claude acceptance claimed.

clarity.evidence: A familiar three-by-three board introduces one move, turn and result before classes.

scope.evidence: A complete fixed-size game uses a small synchronized aggregate, not a framework or unnecessary pattern hierarchy.

contracts.evidence: Immutable snapshots, expected version and private board keep callers from changing a game outside its move boundary.

correctness.evidence: 119800 checks traverse 5478 legal positions and include final-square wins, invalid moves and a same-version race.

failure_handling.evidence: Invalid moves preserve turn/version; stale versions cannot change the board; finished games reject later moves.

tradeoffs.evidence: Scanning the latest row/column versus counters and optimistic versions versus locks are answered at the fixed-size scope.

visual_learning.evidence: Recorded Java histories show placement and rejected moves; a separately labelled browser play mode allows invalid/stale requests.

code.evidence: examples/learning-java/src/kb/tictactoe; full copyable source/download parity and exact excerpts checked by check_review_lot.py; actual runtime output in lot-command-output.json and lot-runtime.json.

rendering.evidence: LLD-16-browser.json: article and walkthrough in light/dark at 1280/390px; theme controls, navigation, no missing images/page-wide overflow, table contrast >=4.5. Per-topic assets resolve.

limits: Local mechanism and fixture checks do not establish remote-provider behavior, distributed durability/failover, production throughput or model quality. Scope-specific boundaries are explicit in the answer.
